Subject: Acme procurement: PO restrictions / prepay path?

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and a couple of follow-ups so we can map the right commercial path.

Call recap:
- Primary use case: internal apps for search/summarization (prod).
- Expected monthly run-rate: ~$12k/month first year, likely scaling.
- Security ask: SOC2 evidence review in progress (Marissa is on this).
- Procurement constraint you mentioned: standard policy may not allow new vendor POs for SaaS without marketplace or prepay.

A few asks so we can qualify:
1) Can you confirm whether Acme will accept a prepay/invoice for the first year vs. an open PO?
2) Would Acme consider purchasing via a cloud marketplace (AWS Marketplace / GCP Marketplace) instead?
3) If a PO is required, any sample terms (payment timeline, GL code, contact) you can share?

If you have a procurement policy PDF handy, that would help speed internal approvals — I can loop Legal/Finance to ask for an exception if needed. Proposed next step: 30-min procurement sync this week if it helps.

Thanks — I’ll also loop Ben and Rishi on the backend to scope any exception path.

Best,

From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>

Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme procurement: PO restrictions / prepay path?

Hi Neha — thanks for the clear recap. Correct on the policy: new SaaS vendors are typically onboarded via one of these three paths only:
- Cloud marketplace (preferred for security/compliance visibility)
- Corporate card payment (for smaller contracts)
- Prepaid invoice for first term while vendor completes vendor security onboarding

We generally do not issue open POs to new vendors unless they are already in our vendor master. For strategic vendors we can discuss creating a standing PO after the first paid term and after security checks.

I attached our procurement policy excerpt that covers payment paths and thresholds. A few specifics from our side:
- Minimum spend to qualify for standing PO: $50k/year
- Prepay acceptable for up to 12 months if vendor provides bank/invoice info and a short MSA addendum
- Marketplace purchase preferred for SaaS where available

We’re happy to meet procurement-side on Thursday to talk details.

Thanks,
Sarah Lee
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme Corp
sarah.lee@acme.com

Forwarding Acme's note and policy excerpt. TL;DR: they don't issue PO for new SaaS vendors unless spend > $50k/yr OR vendor is in vendor master. They will accept prepay for first year or marketplace purchase.

Asking:
- Can Legal/Finance approve an initial prepay invoice + short MSA addendum as a standard exception?
- If we pursue marketplace path, what is the ETA for listing (AWS/GCP)? Any blockers from our side?

Attached policy from Acme for context. I think a short 1-page MSA addendum + prepay invoice (NET 0) could be the fastest path to close while security completes SOC2 checks.

Scheduling: Sarah suggested Thursday for a procurement sync (she's flexible in the morning PT). Can we aim to prep a draft addendum before then?

Thanks — Neha

Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme procurement: PO restrictions / prepay path?

Thanks for flagging Neha — good catch. Proposed approach:
1) Marketplace: Confirm whether Acme prefers AWS Marketplace. If yes, we can fast-track a listing but it typically takes 2-4 weeks depending on billing setup. Not the fastest for a near-term close.
2) Prepay/invoice: We can do a one-time prepay invoice for the first 12 months (NET 0). Finance will need to approve the receivable and Rishi/Legal to sign a 1-page MSA addendum limiting liability and confirming service details.
3) PO exception: If they want standing PO, they'll need to hit the $50k/yr threshold or get vendor-master onboarding (which can be slower).

Action items I can take this week:
- Draft a short MSA addendum for prepay + forward to Rishi for quick review.
- Prepare a sample prepay invoice and GL code mapping for Acme.
- Join procurement call Thursday (suggest 11:00 AM PT) to close on the path.

Neha — can you confirm the expected ARR/first-year commitment so we size the invoice? Sarah mentioned ~$12k/month initial runway — is that correct?
